{{nihongo|'''Kattamine Shrine'''|刈田嶺神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

It is a Shikinai shrine named {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} in "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}," and {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}. It is the largest shrine in the county, and is the general guardian of Katta County and the guardian deity of {{ill|Date clan|ca|Clan Date|de|Date (Klan)|eo|Date (klano)|es|Clan Date|fa|خاندان داته|fr|Clan Date|it|Clan Date|ja|伊達氏|ko|다테씨|pt|Clã Date|ru|Датэ (род)|tr|Date boyu|uk|Рід Дате|zh|伊達氏|qid=Q1151061|lt=Date family}} vassals {{ill|Katakura clan|Q15149847|qid=Q15149847|lt=Katakura family}} ({{ill|Shiroishi Castle|de|Burg Shiroishi|es|Castillo de Shiroishi|fa|قلعه شیروایشی|fr|Château de Shiroishi|ja|白石城|ko|시로이시성|zh|白石城|qid=Q1037902}} lord). Another name is ``Shiratori Daimyojin.''

== Enshrined God ==
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japan Takeru}}
In {{ill|Katta District, Miyagi|ceb|Katta-gun|fr|District de Katta|id|Distrik Katta, Miyagi|it|Distretto di Katta|ja|刈田郡|ko|갓타군|pl|Powiat Katta|ru|Катта (уезд)|sr|Област Ката|uk|Повіт Катта|zh|刈田郡|zh_yue|刈田郡|qid=Q1131771}}, where our company is located, and in the neighboring {{ill|Shibata District, Miyagi|Q1131788|qid=Q1131788}}, there is a ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=swan}} faith,'' and it is said that there are many swan {{ill|Ema (Shinto)|ar|إما (شنتو)|cs|Ema (šintoismus)|da|Ema|de|Ema|el|Έμα (Σίντο)|es|Ema (sintoísmo)|fa|اما (شینتو)|fr|Ema|hu|Ema|id|Ema (Shinto)|it|Ema (Shinto)|ja|絵馬|jv|Ema (Shinto)|ko|에마 (신토)|nl|Ema (Shinto)|pl|Ema (shintō)|ru|Эма|sv|Ema|tr|Ema|uk|Ема|zh|繪馬|qid=Q687288}} dedicated to our company.<ref>[http://www.dokitan.com/sitei/25.html Kattamine Shrine Ema] (Zao Town Board of Education)</ref><ref>[https://www.town.shibata.miyagi.jp/index.cfm/81,27038,154,279,html Shiratori Incident and the Shibata Family] (Shibata Town)</ref><ref>``Murata Town History''</ref>. There is also a group of ancient Shiratori monuments on the grounds. For the relationship between Shiratori and Takeru Nihon, please refer to the corresponding article.

== History ==
The auspicious origins of Kattamine Shrine<ref name="#1">Ryuho Jitsumasa Yasuon Kunshu 1716 "Mutsu Katta County Soja Shiratori Myojin Origin" (Reprinted in "Zao Town History Materials Part II" by Zao Town History Compilation Committee 1989)</ref> b>To</sub>say<sub>fu</sub>persons have<sub>ri</sub>'' and ``舊<sub>TO</sub>mine<sub>ノ</sub>Shrine<sub>to</sub>號<sub>su</sub>''.
At that time, Mt. Aoma was called ``Okattayama,'' and it is the origin of Kattamine Shrine. At the Zuishinmon Gate ({{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}}10 ​​(1827)), there is a vertical plaque that reads ``Mine Shrine.'' {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}}{{ill|Yōrō|Q1373061|qid=Q1373061}} From the Shiroishi side where the county residence of Katta District, founded in 722, is located. The view of Mt. Aoma is the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=twin-eared peak}} of ``Mt. Akera'' (820m) and ``Mt. Aoma'' (799m). It closely resembles {{ill|Mount Tsukuba|Q1754619|qid=Q1754619}} (Mt. Nyotai 877m, Mt. Nantai 871m), and the oldest belief in Kattamine deity is Mt. Aoma. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mt. Shintai}} <ref>Nobumitsu Katakura, 1957, “Okatta Sanroku Essays,” Sendai Local Studies Vol. 17, No. 1, pp. 52-58</ref>.In {{ill|Shibata District, Miyagi|Q1131788|qid=Q1131788}} and {{ill|Katta District, Miyagi|ceb|Katta-gun|fr|District de Katta|id|Distrik Katta, Miyagi|it|Distretto di Katta|ja|刈田郡|ko|갓타군|pl|Powiat Katta|ru|Катта (уезд)|sr|Област Ката|uk|Повіт Катта|zh|刈田郡|zh_yue|刈田郡|qid=Q1131771}}, there is a ``Swan Legend'' related to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Takeru}}. There are several shrines that remain, and according to old legend, when Takeru Takeru, the second son of Emperor Keiko, was on his eastern expedition, Takeru moved to Kumabono in Seishu. She died, turned into a swan and flew away, and enshrined Shiratori Myojin where she landed, or {{ill|Emperor Yōmei|Q349281|qid=Q349281}}'s daughter {{ill|Princess Hashihito no Anahobe|Q11597250|qid=Q11597250}} (mother of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}}) died in this area, turned into a swan, and the local people enshrined a shrine <ref name="#1"/><ref>{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sakuma Dogan}}1719 "Ou Kansekimon Roshi" Volume 4</ref>. There is a legend that the second son of Japan Takeru, {{ill|Emperor Chūai|Q179971|qid=Q179971}}, ordered the lord of Katta County to build a shrine on the western mountain of Katta, where a swan perched.<ref name="#1"/>.In {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, in the 20th year (801) of {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}}, {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|Q941979|qid=Q941979}} invaded Ezo. When they prayed for the pacification of the Toi at the Nishinomiya Shrine (enshrined deity: Nihon Takeru) during the logging, Prince Myonen Daito ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ani Ryutame}}) and Lord Bangu ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mothere}}) surrendered, and the remnants were slaughtered and released into exile. At this time, the shogun transferred Mine no Kami to the hall of the West Palace, where it was enshrined as a shrine. A small fable enshrining a wooden statue of Yakushi was built in the ruins of the Mine Shrine, and this led to the mountain being named ``Yakushigatake.''<ref name="#1"/>{{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} In the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Jōgan tsunami}} caused by the Mutsu Province Earthquake on May 26, 869, Karitamine was appointed as the Junior Fourth Rank Lower on December 8 of the same year, and again on December 25. In Sakuma Togan's 1719 ``Ou Kansekimon Roshi,'' the rank of the lower deity of Jushimi was super-rank, questioning the fact that Karita Mine no Kami was super-rank in December 1997, and suggested that there may have been some omission of facts during this time. </ref> (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}''), and at the time, this great earthquake and tsunami was considered to be a ``sacred ritual caused by the wonders of the volcano.'' This is said to be because it was interpreted as being caused by the ``wrath of the mountain god.''<ref>Togo Yoshida, 1906, ``The 11th year of Jokan, the earthquake and flood of Mutsufu Castle,'' Historical Geography, Vol. 8, No. 1, pp. 1-8</ref>. It is difficult to think that Mt. Aoma exhibited some kind of divine power (volcanic activity), and the "Karita Mine" mentioned in "{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}}" is attached to the summit of Zao. It seems to be referring to the vicinity of the nearby crater.<ref>Junichi Aihara 2018 "Tagajo and Jogan Tsunami" Archeology Magazine Vol. 101 No. 1, Archaeological Society of Japan, pp. 1-53. </ref>. ``Zao Daigongen Shrine'' (Okumiya) of Kattamine Shrine, which is currently enshrined on Mt. Kattadake, and later ``Zao Daigongen Otabigu Shrine'' (Satomiya Shrine) in Togatta, are not only the enshrined deity ``Zao Daigongen,'' but also ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ten Water God}}'' and ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kokusui God}}, which are positioned as the gods in charge of the water of heaven and earth throughout Mutsu Province.At the end of the Heian period, it was under the protection of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|Q3082851|qid=Q3082851}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|Q32613|qid=Q32613}}, and {{ill|Northern Fujiwara|ar|فوجيوارا الشمالية|cs|Severní Fudžiwarové|fa|خاندان فوجیوارای شمالی|ff|Northern Fujiwara|fr|Ōshū Fujiwara|ja|奥州藤原氏|ko|오슈 후지와라씨|pt|Clã Ōshū Fujiwara|ru|Северные Фудзивара|uk|Муцівські Фудзівара|zh|奧州藤原氏|qid=Q1050942}}, but with the fall of the Oshu Fujiwara clan, it lost its protectors, and it is said that Minamoto no Yoritomo left it ``scattered left and right with rubble, with nowhere to put its feet.''<ref name="#1"/>. During the year {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|cs|Eišó|fa|ایشو (دوره موروماچی)|fr|Ère Eishō (Muromachi)|ja|永正|ko|에이쇼 (센고쿠 시대)|no|Eishō (Sengoku)|ru|Эйсё|simple|Eishō (Muromachi period)|sr|Еишо (Муромачи период)|sv|Eishō (Sengoku)|tr|Eishō (Muromachi)|zh|永正|qid=Q1193577}}, the chief priest's distant grandson Shokan Sato had the will to restore the area, and since Nishinomiya belonged to the ancient path and was no longer accessible to local residents, he moved Nishinomiya to the northwest of Miyamura (current location). By the end of {{ill|Bunroku|Q1373039|qid=Q1373039}}, it was once again in ruins, and local residents were downsizing it and rebuilding it as a small shrine. {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} In 1600, Date Masamune attacked Shiroishi Castle and made Katakura Kagetsuna the lord of Shiroishi Castle. Kagetsuna designated Miyarenzo-ji Temple as his Bettoji Temple, and decided to rebuild a major shrine from the devastation of the shrine. In 1611, the second generation, Shigenaga, carried out the wishes of his predecessor, cleaning out the old shrine and renovating the various halls. He appointed Kanzai as a Sengu doshi, gave him 20 koku of temple territory, and made Bettoji Renzo-ji Temple the Katakura family's temple for the blessings of disaster relief.<ref name="#1"/>The == History of company name ==
The company names are ``Reine <sub>no</sub> Shrine'' (``Mutsu Katta County Soja Shiratori Myojin Engiki'', 1716) and ``Shiratori Myojin'' (``Mutsu Katta County Soja Shiratori Myojin Engiki'', 1716). (2010), ``Katta{{Ruby|Shrine|Miya}}'' (by local people, this is called ``Kattamiya Shrine''.There is a temple called Takarachiyama Renzo-ji Temple on the south side of the shrine, and according to both legends, it is mentioned in the Shinmecho. The Karutamine Shrine in Tokoro is not actually the shrine of this shrine.On the other hand, there are doubts about the Chokan 11th year of the reign of Karutamine. It is called Mt. Fubo, and since there is Zao Gongen Shrine on the mountain, it is called Zao Dake. }} Lists the volcanic activity in Zao in 1999 (Ou Kanseimon Roshi, 1719), Kattamine Shrine (1719). ``Hounai Meisekishi'' (1741), ``Katamine Shrine'' (``Hunai Fudoki'', 1772), ``Shoichii Shiratori Daimyo Shrine'' (``Engishiki Jinmyocho Nisōdai Kō Katta District Ichizamine Shrine Nigozako. ``Okoha Okatta Yamanouchi Gojinza Ari no Koro,'' ``Yasunaga Fudoki Goyosho Deri'' (1777), June 10, 1872, {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} It was listed as a local shrine, and on March 1, 1907, it was designated as a Shinto shrine and a designated shrine, and on November 9, 1928, in the Godaiten, it was listed as a prefectural shrine.Due to the defeat in the {{ill|Boshin War|ar|حرب بوشين|arz|حرب بوشين|ast|Guerra Boshin|az|Boşin müharibəsi|azb|بوشین ساواشی|be|Вайна Басін|bg|Война Бошин|bn|বোশিন যুদ্ধ|br|Brezel ar Boshin|ca|Guerra Boshin|cs|Válka Bošin|da|Boshinkrigen|de|Boshin-Krieg|el|Πόλεμος Μπόσιν|eo|Boŝin-milito|es|Guerra Boshin|et|Boshini sõda|eu|Boshin Gerra|fa|جنگ بوشین|fi|Boshin-sota|fr|Guerre de Boshin|gl|Guerra Boshin|he|מלחמת בושין|hu|Bosin-háború|hy|Բոշին պատերազմ|ia|Guerra de Boshin|id|Perang Boshin|it|Guerra Boshin|ja|戊辰戦争|ka|ბოშინის ომი|ko|보신 전쟁|lt|Bošino karas|ms|Perang Boshin|nl|Boshinoorlog|no|Boshinkrigen|pl|Wojna boshin|pt|Guerra Boshin|ru|Война Босин|simple|Boshin War|sl|Bošinska vojna|sr|Бошин рат|sv|Boshinkriget|th|สงครามโบชิน|tl|Digmaang Boshin|tr|Boshin Savaşı|uk|Війна Босін|vi|Chiến tranh Boshin|zh|戊辰戰爭|zh_yue|戊辰戰爭|qid=Q309184}}, in 1870, the former lord of Shiroishi Castle, Katakura Kojuro Kuninori, ordered over 150 of his former vassals to join him. He moved to Horobetsu District, Shunkoku, and enshrined a branch spirit of Japan Takeru, the deity enshrined at Kattamine Shrine, the general guardian deity of the Katakura clan, and enshrined it at the local Myoken Inari Shrine, making it the guardian deity of the development of Horobetsu District. In 1871, a new shrine building was erected at Hama-Nanaju, Horobetsu Village, and the company name was changed to {{ill|Katta Shrine|ja|刈田神社 (登別市)|qid=Q17226399|lt=Katta Shrine}}.
